choices.text: Only renaming the logical view.

choices.text: Giving analysts Project Owner.
choices.html: Giving analysts Project Owner.

choices.html: Moving the query text into an email.

text: The training pipeline scales features using fitted training statistics. What should serving use?
html: The training pipeline scales features using fitted training statistics. What should serving use?

choices.text: A random feature order on every request.
choices.html: A random feature order on every request.
choices.why: Changing feature alignment can invalidate predictions.

choices.text: The same fitted transformation and parameters.
choices.html: The same fitted transformation and parameters.
choices.why: Consistent fitted preprocessing avoids training-serving skew.

choices.text: New independently fitted statistics for every request.
choices.html: New independently fitted statistics for every request.
choices.why: That changes the meaning of model input.

choices.text: Unprocessed values because the model is deployed.
choices.html: Unprocessed values because the model is deployed.
choices.why: Deployment does not remove the learned input contract.

choices.text: A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule.

choices.text: Data leakage from information unavailable at prediction time.

choices.text: Too few dashboard colors.

text: A supported daily sales aggregation is queried by hundreds of dashboards. You want reuse with low maintenance while preserving the required freshness. Which two checks are needed before choosing a materialized view? (Choose 2.)
html: A supported daily sales aggregation is queried by hundreds of dashboards. You want reuse with low maintenance while preserving the required freshness. Which two checks are needed before choosing a materialized view? (Choose 2.)

choices.text: That a logical view is always physically stored as the same aggregate.
choices.html: That a logical view is always physically stored as the same aggregate.
choices.why: A logical view stores a definition, not automatically a precomputed result.

choices.text: That selecting a larger chart font eliminates repeated SQL work.
choices.html: That selecting a larger chart font eliminates repeated SQL work.
choices.why: Presentation style does not establish aggregate reuse.

choices.text: Whether the query shape and selected materialized-view mode are supported.
choices.html: Whether the query shape and selected materialized-view mode are supported.
choices.why: Supported definitions and refresh behavior constrain the design.

choices.text: Whether the full data-to-dashboard freshness contract is satisfied.
choices.html: Whether the full data-to-dashboard freshness contract is satisfied.
choices.why: Precomputed results do not remove upstream or presentation-side freshness concerns.

explanation: A materialized-view decision depends on supported query semantics and the required refresh behavior. Measure repeated-query latency and end-to-end freshness separately.
reviewNote: Original applied learning scenario, reviewed against the linked primary references. It is not an official exam item.

text: A dashboard refreshes every minute but shows hour-old figures. The warehouse query runs quickly. Which next investigation is best supported?
html: A dashboard refreshes every minute but shows hour-old figures. The warehouse query runs quickly. Which next investigation is best supported?

choices.text: Trace source ingestion, aggregate refresh and presentation caching timestamps.
choices.html: Trace source ingestion, aggregate refresh and presentation caching timestamps.
choices.why: Fast execution and frequent dashboard refresh do not prove the upstream data is fresh.

choices.text: Assume one-minute presentation refresh guarantees one-minute event freshness.
choices.html: Assume one-minute presentation refresh guarantees one-minute event freshness.
choices.why: The refresh operates on the data made available to it.

choices.text: Buy more slots immediately because every freshness problem is compute starvation.
choices.html: Buy more slots immediately because every freshness problem is compute starvation.
choices.why: The stated fast query does not establish that hypothesis.

choices.text: Remove all access controls to refresh faster.
choices.html: Remove all access controls to refresh faster.
choices.why: That does not address the observed timestamp gap and changes the security contract.

explanation: End-to-end freshness spans event occurrence, ingestion, transformation and display. A fast query over stale inputs can return an old business state very efficiently.
reviewNote: Original applied learning scenario, reviewed against the linked primary references. It is not an official exam item.

text: A classifier catches 8 of 10 actual positive cases and raises 12 positive alerts in total. Which statement is correct?
html: A classifier catches 8 of 10 actual positive cases and raises 12 positive alerts in total. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Both measures must equal overall accuracy.
choices.html: Both measures must equal overall accuracy.
choices.why: Accuracy uses a different denominator and needs additional population counts.

choices.text: Recall is 80% and precision is about 66.7%.
choices.html: Recall is 80% and precision is about 66.7%.
choices.why: Recall is 8/10; precision is 8/12.

choices.text: Precision is 80% and recall is about 66.7%.
choices.html: Precision is 80% and recall is about 66.7%.
choices.why: That swaps the actual-positive and predicted-positive denominators.

choices.text: The positive-alert total alone proves there are no false positives.
choices.html: The positive-alert total alone proves there are no false positives.
choices.why: Twelve alerts with eight true positives implies four false positives.

explanation: Use the correct denominator for each business error. Recall asks how many actual positives were found; precision asks how many predicted positives were true. Overall accuracy cannot be computed from these counts alone.

text: A demand forecast is evaluated with a random row split that lets future records for the same products influence training preprocessing. Which two changes should be considered? (Choose 2.)
html: A demand forecast is evaluated with a random row split that lets future records for the same products influence training preprocessing. Which two changes should be considered? (Choose 2.)

choices.text: Add future final sales totals to improve the reported validation score.
choices.html: Add future final sales totals to improve the reported validation score.
choices.why: That strengthens leakage rather than producing a realistic evaluation.

choices.text: Treat a higher validation score as proof the split is valid.
choices.html: Treat a higher validation score as proof the split is valid.
choices.why: A high score can itself be inflated by leakage.

choices.text: Fit preprocessing on training information and reuse its parameters.
choices.html: Fit preprocessing on training information and reuse its parameters.
choices.why: Evaluation and serving should not introduce future information into fitted transformations.

choices.text: Use a deployment-relevant temporal or entity-aware evaluation design.
choices.html: Use a deployment-relevant temporal or entity-aware evaluation design.
choices.why: The holdout should reflect information available at prediction time.

explanation: The issue is whether evaluation represents deployment, not whether a random split is syntactically valid. Prevent information leakage through time, repeated entities and fitted preprocessing.

text: A company restricts some policy documents. A RAG service retrieves relevant chunks before calling a model. Which two controls belong before or within the retrieval-to-generation boundary? (Choose 2.)
html: A company restricts some policy documents. A RAG service retrieves relevant chunks before calling a model. Which two controls belong before or within the retrieval-to-generation boundary? (Choose 2.)

choices.text: Treat a high vector similarity as proof that the user has access.
choices.html: Treat a high vector similarity as proof that the user has access.
choices.why: Similarity is not an authorization decision.

choices.text: Preserve document identity and version for traceable citations.
choices.html: Preserve document identity and version for traceable citations.
choices.why: A useful answer needs provenance and freshness context.

choices.text: Apply authorization so the model receives only permitted chunks.
choices.html: Apply authorization so the model receives only permitted chunks.
choices.why: Authorization should prevent forbidden evidence from entering the context.

choices.text: Retrieve every restricted document and trust final redaction alone.
choices.html: Retrieve every restricted document and trust final redaction alone.
choices.why: That has already exposed the restricted material to the generation path.

explanation: Retrieval relevance, authorization and provenance are separate requirements. A semantically useful passage is not automatically permitted, and a generated citation is only meaningful when the source can be traced.

text: A RAG answer cites a real document but draws a conclusion not supported by its passages. Which evaluation is needed?
html: A RAG answer cites a real document but draws a conclusion not supported by its passages. Which evaluation is needed?

choices.text: Increase embedding dimensionality as a universal correctness fix.
choices.html: Increase embedding dimensionality as a universal correctness fix.
choices.why: That is not evidence that the unsupported conclusion will be repaired.

choices.text: Evaluate answer groundedness separately from retrieval relevance and citation existence.
choices.html: Evaluate answer groundedness separately from retrieval relevance and citation existence.
choices.why: A real citation does not prove that the generated conclusion follows from the evidence.

choices.text: Only check that a URL appears somewhere in the response.
choices.html: Only check that a URL appears somewhere in the response.
choices.why: Citation syntax does not establish faithful interpretation.

choices.text: Assume a vector index guarantees factual answers.
choices.html: Assume a vector index guarantees factual answers.
choices.why: An index helps retrieval and does not validate every generated statement.

explanation: Assess useful, permitted retrieval and faithful generation as different layers. Trace whether the actual supporting passage was retrieved and whether the conclusion is justified by it.

text: An external partner should query a permitted regional aggregation without receiving direct access to raw customer tables. Which design best expresses that requirement?
html: An external partner should query a permitted regional aggregation without receiving direct access to raw customer tables. Which design best expresses that requirement?

choices.text: Expose an appropriately authorized view or governed data product containing the permitted result.
choices.html: Expose an appropriately authorized view or governed data product containing the permitted result.
choices.why: The consumer should receive the approved shape through a controlled access path.

choices.text: Email an unrestricted service account key for the raw project.
choices.html: Email an unrestricted service account key for the raw project.
choices.why: A broad credential does not enforce the intended data subset.

choices.text: Give every partner direct access to the raw bucket regardless of the table design.
choices.html: Give every partner direct access to the raw bucket regardless of the table design.
choices.why: That bypasses the stated restriction on raw data.

choices.text: Grant project-wide Editor and rely on a dashboard filter for secrecy.
choices.html: Grant project-wide Editor and rely on a dashboard filter for secrecy.
choices.why: That exposes broader underlying access than the approved result.

explanation: Choose an access path that exposes the permitted data shape and preserves producer control. Sharing a report or credential is not a substitute for enforcing the underlying data policy.
